title: Cost-Latency Z-Score Rollback Detector for Mixed-Cohort Canaries
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Implement an automated rollback trigger tuned for canary/A-B/shadow workflows that combines latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput into a single, interpretable detection signal. Target use cases: short-lived canaries (5-30 minutes), A/B experiments with unequal cohort sizes, and shadow traffic verification runs. The detector must minimize false positives on traffic spikes and cost blips while ensuring fast rollback for regressions that harm latency or correctness.

Motivation: Existing single-metric thresholds (e.g., 95th latency or error rate) are brittle when traffic mixes cohorts or when token-cost anomalies occur. We need a composite detector that normalizes signals per-cohort, adapts thresholds to baseline drift, and uses hysteresis to prevent oscillation during noisy windows.
acceptance_criteria: Composite z-score is computed for each canary cohort combining latency, error_rate, and normalized token_cost with configurable weights
Detector raises a rollback recommendation within 3 minutes of a genuine SLO regression in synthetic canary tests (simulated + live shadow)
False positive rate <= 2% on 48h historical replay of production traffic with injected benign spikes
Rollback action respects existing rollout policies (canary percentage floor, cooldown windows) and logs a reproducible signal summary to the rollout audit trail
Operator UI shows per-cohort z-scores and contributing metrics, and exposes a slider to tune metric weights and hysteresis settings
tasks: Design z-score composition and per-metric normalization strategy (latency quantiles, error-rate binomial correction, cost per-token normalization)
Prototype detector in Python using historical metrics exporter and replay harness
Integrate detector as a runtime webhook for rollout controller with non-blocking effect (recommendation + enabled auto-rollback flag)
Add operator controls to Console: weights, z-thresholds, min-traffic floor, cooldown/hysteresis parameters
Create e2e canary test harness (shadow traffic replay, synthetic regressions) and run 48h replay experiments
Document playbook for on-call: how to interpret signal, override, and perform manual rollback
design_decisions: Use z-score aggregation across standardized metric streams rather than raw thresholds to adapt to baseline drift
Normalize token_cost per request using a rolling median of cost-per-token for the model family to avoid punishing high-token workloads
Apply a cohort-aware baseline window (rolling 3h) instead of global product-wide baselines to account for regional and cohort traffic patterns
Hysteresis implemented as a two-tier system: an immediate soft-alert at z>3 (visible in Console) and a hard auto-rollback at sustained z>4 for 3 consecutive minutes OR z>5 for any single 30s window
Avoid heavy Bayesian posterior sampling in the hot path to keep the detector sub-500ms decision latency; use lightweight approximate stats for live checks and async posterior refinement for analytics
tradeoffs: Pros: adaptive to drift, interpretable contributor scores for operators, robust to single-metric noise
Cons: requires good baseline windows and reliable metric ingestion; small cohorts (<200 requests/min) have noisier z-scores and may need larger smoothing windows
Operational cost: additional metric cardinality (cohort x metric) will slightly increase TSDB storage and compute for the real-time aggregator
implementation_notes: Live test harness: replay job canary-replay-2026-03 on datalab cluster (job id: replay-20260305-01)
Webhook contract: rollout-controller accepts 'rollback_recommendation' with fields: reason, composite_z, contributors[] (Console expects simple CSV of top contributors)
Minimum traffic floor default: 100 req/min per cohort for auto-rollback; below that only surface recommendations to operators
risks_mitigation: Risk: oscillations on bursty traffic -> mitigation: cooldown window 10m and min-traffic floor
Risk: inaccurate cost normalization with new quantization settings -> mitigation: export quantization profile telemetry and fallback to model-family median
Risk: delayed detection if metric pipeline lags -> mitigation: healthcheck on pipeline lag and auto-disable auto-rollback if lag > 30s
